chunks: He has seen his way, and walked his path, and known his beacon, and crossed his deep waters.
He has held fast to the most secure ties, and from the ropes the strongest, so he is of certainty upon the like of the light of the sun.
He has set himself for Allah, the Glorified, in the highest of matters, from dismissing every incoming thought to him, and directing every branch to its root.
Lamp of darkness, remover of veils, key to obscurities, remover of complexities, guide in vast deserts.
He speaks so he makes understood, and he remains silent so it is safe.
He has purified himself for Allah so He purified him; he is from the mines of His faith, and the stakes of His earth.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual characteristics of a true believer according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha is often interpreted as describing the ideal state of the Imam or the perfected believer, whose intellect and heart are illuminated by divine certainty (yaqin). The metaphor of 'removing obscurities' (kashshaf ghawat) aligns with the concept of the Imam as the interpreter of the Quran's esoteric meanings, ensuring that religious rulings are derived from their authentic roots. This spiritual elevation transforms the believer into a stable 'peg' (awtad) of the earth, embodying both intellectual clarity and practical guidance.
